---
description: "How to keep NCodeGroup services and front ends fast and bounded: hot-path allocations and I/O, caching (including cache correctness and freshness), bounded background and request work, AOT safety, static asset delivery and front-end bundle splitting."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.csproj, **/*.props, **/.editorconfig, **/vite.config.*, **/*.ts, **/*.mts, **/*.tsx"
---

# Performance

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Optimize cryptographic and numeric hot-path primitives as much as you like (AggressiveInlining/AggressiveOptimization, unrolling, stackalloc, `MemoryMarshal`/`Unsafe` zero-copy access, bounds-check elision), but never add a data-dependent branch or memory access to constant-time code, and keep test vectors and differential tests covering every optimized path.** These primitives are performance-critical, but speed must never cost constant-time behavior or correctness. *Check:* Look for data-dependent branches, early exits or secret-indexed lookups added to constant-time code, and for optimizations that no test vector or differential test covers. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not cache authorization-relevant data (roles, permissions, server-owned metadata that ends up in tokens) in a per-node `IMemoryCache` or an in-process dictionary. Read it fresh from the store by default. If it must be cached, add an opt-in, replaceable decorator over `IDistributedCache` that is invalidated when the security stamp changes.** In a cluster, a per-node cache lets different nodes make different authorization decisions for the same principal. Reading fresh keeps the store as the single source of truth. *Check:* Look for `IMemoryCache` or static/in-process dictionaries holding data that drives authorization or token contents, or for a built-in freshness setting for that data where an opt-in distributed-cache decorator belongs. <sub>Identity ADR-0055</sub>
- **Cache revocation data only after it is parsed, verified and current. Key a CRL by its location and the issuer's SHA-256 thumbprint, key an OCSP response by location, issuer and serial number, and expire each entry at the earlier of its `nextUpdate` and a configured maximum cache duration.** Revocation data must never be served past its `nextUpdate`. The cap bounds staleness, and including the issuer in the key stops one issuer's data from being reused for another. *Check:* Look for revocation cache entries with no expiry, an expiry past `nextUpdate` or no maximum cap; CRL keys made of the URL alone or using a SHA-1 thumbprint; OCSP keys missing the issuer or serial; or data cached before it is verified. *Note:* ADR-0259 describes CRL keys as per location only. ADR-0173's more specific requirement to also key by the issuer's SHA-256 thumbprint is kept. <sub>Identity ADR-0173; Identity ADR-0259</sub>
- **Cache remote protocol metadata and key sets (such as `jwks_uri`) per URI with an absolute expiration bounded by the configured duration. On a failed refresh, the cache may serve its last good value within a bounded stale lifetime, but it must never relax validation to do so. It must collapse concurrent misses into one fetch, rate-limit forced refreshes (for example on an unknown `kid`), and throw when the first fetch fails.** Caching keeps verification from fetching on every request and still allows key rotation. It keeps the client available during brief provider outages without weakening security or hammering the provider. *Check:* Look for metadata or key fetches made on every validation; caches with no absolute expiration or not keyed by URI; validation skipped for stale values; concurrent misses that each fetch; unlimited forced refreshes; or a fabricated value when the first fetch fails. <sub>Identity ADR-0106; Identity ADR-0270</sub>
- **Treat a cache-invalidation broadcast as a hint only. Every cache it invalidates must still have a bounded absolute lifetime or a polling fallback.** Broadcasts can be lost, so a replica that missed one must still converge. A sliding expiration alone can keep a busy entry stale forever. *Check:* Look for caches that rely only on broadcast or pub/sub invalidation, or that use only a sliding expiration with no absolute lifetime or periodic refresh. <sub>Identity ADR-0205</sub>
- **Fetch remote revocation data (CRLs, OCSP) only from http/https locations, through a guarded named `HttpClient` with a fetch timeout and a maximum response size. Share concurrent retrievals of the same key, and remember failed retrievals and failing responders in the in-replica cache for a failure duration.** Revocation checks run inside client authentication, so each retrieval must stay bounded and shared, and an outage should cost one timeout per replica and responder, not one per request. *Check:* Look for revocation HTTP calls without the named client, timeout or size limit; redirects or schemes other than http/https being followed; duplicate concurrent fetches; failures that are not remembered; or this cache shared across replicas. <sub>Identity ADR-0259</sub>
- **When several counters must be checked in order and processing must stop at the first refusal, run them as one atomic server-side script, not as sequential calls, a pipeline, or increment-then-compensate decrements.** Sequential calls cost a round trip each, and a pipeline cannot stop at the first refusal. Compensating decrements leave over-counts that refuse other callers and that remain if a replica stops partway. *Check:* Look for sequential awaits to the counter store for each limit in one request, pipelined increments of dependent limits, or decrement-to-undo logic after a refusal. <sub>Identity ADR-0246</sub>
- **Never run work that grows with the size of the deployment (a pass over every tenant, client or other unbounded set) inside a request or on a bounded in-process job dispatcher. Run it as a background reconciliation over an untracked, secret-free projection that skips entities the change cannot affect.** Such passes make request latency unbounded and tie up the dispatcher's limited workers. *Check:* Look for request handlers or queued jobs that loop over every tenant, client or other unbounded entity set. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a list endpoint filters by a predicate that must be evaluated in memory, make each request scan one bounded page of the underlying rows and return a continuation token, even when the filtered page is empty. Never scan the whole set in one request.** Otherwise the cost of each request grows with the size of the collection. Callers keep paging until the token is null. *Check:* Look for list handlers that load every row of a collection, filter in memory and return everything at once, or that stop returning a continuation token as soon as a filtered page is empty. <sub>Identity ADR-0233</sub>
- **Back in-memory background work queues with a bounded channel, and log whenever a full queue drops an item.** Bounded back-pressure keeps memory in check, and logging each dropped item makes the loss visible to operators. *Check:* Look for `Channel.CreateUnbounded` or other unbounded queues in background processing, or overflow paths that drop items without logging. <sub>Identity ADR-0090</sub>
- **Return buffered collections by default. Return lazy `IEnumerable`/`IAsyncEnumerable` only for large, I/O-backed or usually short-circuited sequences, and never as a deferred sequence that captures request or ambient context or that callers will enumerate more than once.** A deferred sequence goes stale once the request ends and re-runs its work each time it is enumerated. *Check:* Look for `yield` or deferred LINQ return values that capture request state (HttpContext, scoped services, DbContext) or that callers enumerate more than once. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Mark code paths that build generic types at runtime (`MakeGenericType` and similar reflection) with `[RequiresDynamicCode]` and `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`, and give AOT or trimmed hosts a switch that falls back to a non-reflective path.** Building generic types at runtime is not safe under Native AOT or trimming. *Check:* Look for `MakeGenericType`, `MakeGenericMethod` or similar reflection that lacks those attributes or an AOT fallback. <sub>Identity ADR-0047</sub>
- **Serve content-hashed static files only from a restricted asset root, with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and no per-tenant resolution. Keep the `ETag`/`Last-Modified` validators and range support, and send no cache lifetime on a `404`.** A hashed name always refers to the same content, so the file can be cached forever. Validators alone make the browser revalidate every file on every page load. The restricted root keeps files such as index.html from being served this way, and a 404 must not be cached. *Check:* Look for hashed-asset routes that omit the immutable header, drop validators or range handling, cache not-found responses, resolve a tenant, or serve files outside the asset root. <sub>Identity ADR-0254; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not write to the database on every request for high-frequency bookkeeping. Record counts as an in-memory increment that a background service writes in batches, and throttle activity timestamps (such as last-activity or touch fields) to a minimum write interval.** Writing a row per request puts log-level write load on the database. Batching and throttling cut it to one small unit of work per replica per interval. *Check:* Look for request handlers or filters that insert or update a row, or publish an event, on every request just to count usage or advance a timestamp, without comparing against a minimum interval. <sub>Identity ADR-0199; Identity ADR-0220</sub>
- **On a per-request hot path, when the cache key can be derived from the request alone (configuration, route value), check the cache with that key before any store read. Run store reads and expensive one-time work (such as provisioning or seeding) only in the cache-miss path.** Reading the store just to get the cache key, or provisioning during resolution, makes every request pay the cost the cache was meant to avoid. *Check:* Look for request-path code that awaits a store load and then uses the loaded identifier for a cache lookup when the identifier was available from the request, or for seeding or provisioning calls outside the cache-miss factory. <sub>Identity ADR-0037; Identity ADR-0166</sub>
- **Cache a failed remote retrieval for a configured duration, and don't call the source again while that entry exists. Don't add retry-with-backoff loops on the request path.** Without a failure cache, an unreachable source costs a full timeout on every request. The remembered failure acts as the backoff. *Check:* Look for remote fetches whose failure path caches nothing, so every request retries right away, or for retry/backoff loops added where a failure cache would do. <sub>Identity ADR-0252</sub>
- **Serve JWKS and public-key lookups from cached public keys, and call the remote KMS or vault only for actual signing operations.** Public keys are safe to cache, and each remote call adds a network round trip. *Check:* Look for JWKS or public-key retrieval code that calls the KMS or vault on every request without caching the result. <sub>Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md</sub>
- **Don't query the database again for an entity this unit of work has already loaded. Check the `DbSet.Local` change tracker first in load-then-update flows, and don't add existence checks for entities the request pipeline has already loaded and verified.** Identity resolution returns the tracked instance anyway, and an entity already loaded upstream is known to exist, so a second query is a wasted round trip. *Check:* Look for store code that re-queries an entity the same unit of work is already tracking, or validators that query the store to confirm an owning entity the pipeline has already resolved. <sub>Identity ADR-0012; Identity ADR-0018</sub>
- **Make requests that don't use an optional feature skip reading and writing that feature's persisted state.** Requests that don't use the feature should pay no storage cost for it. *Check:* Look for grant or state writes and lookups that run unconditionally, even when the request did not ask for the feature. <sub>Identity ADR-0039</sub>
- **When a reader needs only a few columns, return a lightweight projection (a narrow SELECT) from the store query instead of the full entity with its child collections.** A projection avoids joining and materializing child collections the caller doesn't use, such as settings or secrets. *Check:* Look for queries that load full entities with `Include()` of child collections when the caller reads only identifiers or a few scalar fields. <sub>Identity ADR-0080</sub>
- **Run an expensive pass over dependent entities after an update only when the update changes a value that the pass reads. Compare the effective values before and after the change first.** An update that changes nothing the pass reads should load nothing, which keeps the cost of updates bounded. *Check:* Look for update handlers that always walk dependent entities without first checking whether the relevant settings changed. <sub>Identity ADR-0204</sub>
- **Do not add a global access-token denylist, reference tokens or per-access-token server state just to support revocation. Revoke by session instead.** Per-token state, with a lookup on every call, brings back the cost that stateless JWTs exist to avoid. *Check:* Look for new stores or tables that record issued access-token identifiers for revocation, or denylist lookups during token validation. <sub>Identity ADR-0112</sub>
- **Do not start a timeout timer (`WaitAsync`, `CancelAfter`) for a `Task`/`ValueTask` that has already completed. Check `IsCompleted` first.** Operations that complete synchronously, such as in-process calls, should start no timer. *Check:* Look for timeout wrappers applied to a task or value task without an `IsCompleted` check first. <sub>Identity ADR-0196</sub>
- **Check whether anything is listening (a subscriber check, in the same way as `ILogger.IsEnabled`) before building an expensive event payload or envelope.** It avoids doing work when no one consumes the result. *Check:* Look for expensive payload or envelope construction before a publish call with no subscriber or listener check. <sub>Identity ADR-0047</sub>
- **When the Request Delegate Generator reports that it cannot generate code for a minimal API handler, change the handler to a supported shape. Do not suppress the diagnostic or disable the generator.** A suppressed diagnostic silently falls back to runtime binding, which compiles expression trees at every host start and brings back the cold-start and JIT cost. *Check:* Look for `#pragma warning disable`, `NoWarn`, `[SuppressMessage]` or `.editorconfig` severity changes aimed at RDG diagnostics, and for `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false` added for any reason other than form-bound endpoints. <sub>Identity ADR-0262</sub>
- **When a client bundle progressively enhances a server-rendered page, have the server embed the data it already knows (such as branding) in the page, and read it synchronously at mount. Do not fetch that data before or after mounting.** Fetching before mounting loses user input or autofill when the page is replaced, and needs a timeout that slow networks exceed. Fetching after mounting paints the page twice with different themes. *Check:* Look for a network request or timeout that gates or follows the first render of an enhanced page for data the host could have embedded, or a new endpoint added only to serve such data. <sub>Identity ADR-0253</sub>
- **Do not raise Vite's `build.chunkSizeWarningLimit` or any similar build threshold to silence a warning. Split the chunk with a vendor code-splitting group or a lazy boundary instead.** Raising the limit hides the problem. A single large chunk delays the first paint and invalidates cached libraries on every app change. *Check:* Look for diffs that raise `chunkSizeWarningLimit` or a chunk-size constant, or that disable or bypass an oversized-chunk check. <sub>Identity ADR-0151; Identity ADR-0175</sub>
- **Import route-level React containers with `React.lazy(() => import(...))` inside a `Suspense` boundary, not with static imports in the app entry or router.** The shell paints before the route loads, and routes that are never visited are never downloaded. *Check:* Look for app entry or router files that statically import route or page container components. <sub>Identity ADR-0175</sub>
- **Configure vendor chunk splitting with Rolldown's `output.codeSplitting.groups`, not the deprecated `manualChunks`, and keep vendor packages in stable groups apart from application code.** `manualChunks` is deprecated in Vite 8. A vendor chunk that changes only when its packages are upgraded stays cached across app releases. *Check:* Look for new uses of `manualChunks`, or chunking rules that mix application modules into vendor groups. <sub>Identity ADR-0175</sub>
- **Reinterpret byte buffers as spans of blittable values with zero-copy `MemoryMarshal` APIs (`Cast`, `AsBytes`, `CreateSpan` with `Unsafe.As`), guarded by `BitConverter.IsLittleEndian` with a `BinaryPrimitives.ReverseEndianness` fallback. Do not use per-element copy loops or `BitConverter` array allocations for this.** Reinterpreting avoids copies and allocations, and the endianness guard, which the JIT treats as a constant, keeps the code correct on every architecture. *Check:* Look for per-element `BinaryPrimitives`/`BitConverter.GetBytes` loops over whole buffers, or `MemoryMarshal.Cast`/`AsBytes` on multi-byte values with no endianness guard and fallback. <sub>Identity ADR-0116</sub>
- **Load a large embedded lookup resource once, lazily on first use, into a frozen collection (for example `FrozenSet<T>`).** This avoids re-reading and re-parsing the resource on each call, and frozen collections are optimized for repeated lookups. *Check:* Look for embedded-resource lookups that re-read or re-parse the resource on each call, or that keep it in a mutable collection. <sub>Identity ADR-0236</sub>
- **Pass a capacity to collection constructors when the final or maximum count is known, return shared empty instances (`[]`, `FrozenSet<T>.Empty`), write `list ?? (IReadOnlyCollection<T>)[]` rather than `list ?? []`, and create collections lazily when they may stay empty.** This avoids resize allocations and empty-collection allocations. `list ?? []` on a `List<T>` allocates a new list. *Check:* Look for `new List<T>()`, `new HashSet<T>()` or `new Dictionary<,>()` without a capacity when the count is known, `?? []` on a list-typed value, or a newly allocated empty collection being returned. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **On per-request paths, use `foreach` loops instead of LINQ (`Any`, `All`, `Where(...).ToHashSet()`), and test `Count == 0` first to avoid creating a boxed enumerator.** Each LINQ call allocates a delegate and an enumerator. *Check:* Look for LINQ calls in request-handling code. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **On hot paths, transform identifiers into rented or stack-allocated char spans (for example `MemoryExtensions.ToLowerInvariant(source, destination)`) instead of allocating new strings.** This avoids a string allocation on every call. *Check:* Look for `string.ToLowerInvariant()`, `ToUpperInvariant()` or similar transforms that allocate a string on per-request paths. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
